question.text: Kaveri Venture Fund II (Cat I-VCF) is preparing to launch a new scheme. Which of the following BEST describes the role of the SEBI-registered Merchant Banker in the PPM filing process?

answer.text: The merchant banker distributes units of the AIF to HNI investors through private placement
The merchant banker acts as custodian for demat securities held by the fund

The merchant banker conducts independent due diligence on PPM disclosures, provides a due-diligence certificate, and files the draft PPM with SEBI on behalf of the Sponsor/Manager; the merchant banker must NOT be an associate of the AIF, sponsor, manager or trustee
The merchant banker negotiates placement fees with LPs on behalf of the manager

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular dated 21-Oct-2021, AIFs shall file the Private Placement Memorandum (PPM) with SEBI ONLY through a SEBI-registered Merchant Banker at the time of registration or launching new schemes. The merchant banker conducts independent due diligence of PPM disclosures, issues a due-diligence certificate, and ensures SEBI's comments are incorporated in the final PPM. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, the merchant banker appointed shall not be an associate of the AIF, its sponsor, manager or trustee. The Trap: The distribution distractor confuses merchant banker with placement agent/distributor. The custodian distractor confuses roles. The LP-negotiation distractor confuses with placement agent. A specific change in PPM terms may be filed directly with SEBI (per Circular 29-Apr-2024) — but launch/annual update still goes through merchant banker. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same merchant banker role. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) may test who signs off on PPM disclosures. Merchant banker PPM filing is a post-Oct-2021 requirement — older study material may not reflect it. Manager's Pro-Tip: Build relationships with 2-3 empanelled merchant bankers — PPM filing deadlines cluster (most Cat I/II funds file in Q4/Q1), and a stuck MB capacity can delay your scheme launch by 4-6 weeks. Also: factor the MB due-diligence fee (typically INR 15-25 lakh per scheme) into set-up costs.
